verdict.rationale: Anytype has no explicit AI-training policy or opt-out, but its documented architecture structurally keeps content away from the vendor. Content is end-to-end encrypted with "not even Anytype can see your content" [31, 43]. It is stored locally on device [29, 44], and local-only mode disables the backup node entirely [24, 30]. That implies but never states that user data cannot be used for model training. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that user data is not used to train AI models, documentation of how AI-assistant integrations handle data with respect to training, and independent corroboration.
